section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch8 — Bandura's 4 Stages of Observational Learning
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: According to Bandura, before a child can imitate a teacher's demonstration of cursive handwriting, the child must first:

options.option_text: Pay attention to and accurately perceive the model's demonstration
Already be able to perform the skill perfectly
Have no motivation of any kind

explanation: Attention is the first of Bandura's four stages of observational learning.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch8 — Bandura's 4 Stages of Observational Learning
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student watches a science demonstration on Monday and successfully repeats the procedure from memory on Friday, several days later. This delayed reproduction is possible because of Bandura's second stage:

options.option_text: Retention — mentally storing the observed behaviour as a symbolic representation
Attention only, with no memory storage involved
Motivation only, with no memory storage involved
Reproduction happening instantly with no delay ever possible

explanation: Retention involves encoding the observed behaviour into memory, enabling reproduction even after a time delay.
